headline: A BBC analysis says audiences are starting to prize art made by people as AI content spreads, but doubts that the preference will last.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a well-argued analysis with useful figures, but opinion-led and nothing new has happened.
importance_line: Deezer’s figures on AI-made music feed the argument that audiences still want human-made art, which matters to artists, writers and musicians first, then platforms and publishers deciding whether to label AI work, but the premium rests on opinion and one survey, and the author is unsure it will last.
summary: BBC News reports, in a first-person analysis, that Deezer says 44% of tracks uploaded to the music service are AI-generated and 97% of listeners could not tell the difference, yet more than half of those surveyed said they care whether a human made the music. Economist Daniel Susskind and New Yorker writer Kyle Chayka argue that people value human-made work more as AI spreads, a “human premium”, but the author doubts it will hold, since audiences already accept algorithm-chosen culture.
notes: Full text read. BBC InDepth analysis; Deezer figures attributed, not checked.
